why: Repositories waiting on a first judging pass. [CORPUS-REGISTER-COVERAGE] A repository cannot become a register until a judge has ruled on its pairs, and a judge cannot rule on pairs until a comparison has produced two reports for it — so a repository that is not yet judged still has to be scanned. This file is that queue: the comparison scans every register plus everything here, and `make judging-folder` turns each into a workspace. When the verdicts come back, the repository moves into corpus/register/ and out of this list. Every entry is pinned to a full commit id for the same reason a register is: the judge and the scan must read identical source.

repositories.name: django
repositories.why: The register judges Python only through click, a small CLI library whose duplication is concentrated in its own test suite. Django is the opposite shape - a large, heavily reviewed framework - so a first judging pass here says whether the Python verdicts generalise past one repository or only describe click.

repositories.name: tokio
repositories.why: ripgrep is the only judged Rust register and it judges five pairs, the thinnest in the corpus. Tokio is macro-heavy async Rust, the construct most likely to manufacture false positives, and judging it is what would let the Rust register carry a real body of verdicts.

repositories.name: nest
repositories.why: The TypeScript register is zod, a single-purpose schema library. Nest is decorator-driven application code with a large module surface, so it exercises the TypeScript normalisation that zod never reaches.
